title: Mission Control · Europa Clipper Earth flyby

narration: On Thursday, a spacecraft headed for Jupiter flies right past Earth.
NASA's Europa Clipper launched from Florida in October 2024.
Now, on December third, it comes home, briefly.
It passes about three thousand two hundred kilometres from Earth, closest west of Africa.
That's at 9:14 in the evening, Central European Time.
Why come back? Our gravity works like a slingshot.
It changes the spacecraft's path and adds speed, saving propellant.
On the first, in March 2025, it passed 884 kilometres above Mars to reshape its orbit.

params.label: above Mars, March 2025: the first flyby

narration: Next stop is Jupiter, in April 2030.
Then nearly fifty flybys of Europa, an icy moon with strong evidence of a salty ocean underneath.
Follow for the next mission update.

post.title: A Jupiter spacecraft flies past Earth on 3 December 🛰️🌍
post.description:
NASA's Europa Clipper, launched on 14 October 2024, flies past Earth on Thursday 3 December 2026, about 3,200 km away, with closest approach west of Africa at 21:14 CET (3:14 p.m. EST). Earth's gravity changes its path and speeds it up, a propellant-saving boost. It is the second gravity assist, after a pass 884 km above Mars on 1 March 2025 that reshaped its orbit. It is due to begin orbiting Jupiter in April 2030 and then make nearly 50 flybys of Europa, an icy moon with strong evidence of a saltwater ocean beneath its surface.
